stem.en: One boat nets fish in water 150 metres deep over the continental shelf. Another nets fish far beyond the shelf, in water 900 metres deep. How are their fish sorted?

text.en: Coastal fish at 900 m, oceanic fish at 150 m

feedback.en: These two are swapped. The shallow water over the shelf holds the coastal fish.
150 metres is less than 200 metres and over the shelf, so that fish is coastal, not oceanic.
900 metres is beyond the shelf and deeper than 200 metres, so that fish is oceanic.

text.en: Coastal fish at 150 m, oceanic fish at 900 m

feedback.en: Yes. Coastal fish live within the shelf at 0 to 200 metres, and oceanic fish live beyond it at more than 200 metres.

explanation.en: Coastal or neritic fish live within the continental shelf, at depths of 0 to 200 metres. Oceanic fish live beyond the shelf, at depths of more than 200 metres. So 150 metres gives a coastal fish and 900 metres gives an oceanic fish.

hints.en: Which depth marks the edge of the shelf in this sorting?
